label: copy-phase only; strongest on 2nd copied token of L=3 sequences, else token-dependent (c/m) at t~11-13
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only on steps whose input is a fed-back copy (never on original or delimiter steps, never on recall_idx 0). Its largest activations (top quartile) are on L=3 sequences at step 5, where the output is the last original token and the input is orig(1) (63% precision there, about 26% of activation mass), especially when the input is c, d, m or v. Everything else is diffuse: weak activations in the middle of the copy phase of longer sequences, concentrated at absolute steps t=11-13 (recall_idx 3-5), with a preference for the input tokens c and m (7.7x and 4.8x lift), but only about 4-5% of those steps fire. The best compact disjunction gets dev F1 0.34 and mass recall 0.50. I found no coherent rule.
